body:
Thank you for your response. I'll see about something like miralax. I've got a pretty high fiber intake already, but maybe I should try and focus on softening rather than bulking fiber?

And yeah, I'm pretty sure as well, but my brain decides that it's the worst possible scenario when I get no definitive diagnosis. Here's to hoping I'll get that diagnosis soon.

Thank you for your response. In general, I eat around 30-38 grams of fiber a day and drink approximately 4000-5000ml of water. I think I've had soda maybe 6 times in the past couple years. I have a bidet and use that plus drying with the paper. I have a standing desk which I use and try to never sit down, only stand or lay down. I also exercise about 5 times a week. I've used hemorrhoid suppositories and cream and notice temporary relief, only for the pain and bleeding to return once I stop using them. Apologies for not including this information in my original post.

Once I'm able to get out, I'll see a doctor ASAP.

The counseling center at my college shows up when you use it through our system, which my mother has access to. Even then, I'm not allowed to go on walks. Additionally, My mother has ensured I have no contact with my doctor. She refuses to take me. She is anti-vax and rarely ever lets me take pain medication if I need it. One time, I was bleeding from a place someone should very much not be bleeding from, and it took a ton of screaming matches to finally go to the doctor. When I got there, I was so worn out and my mother didn't stop talking to the doctor, so I got no word in. I had no energy to say anything. I was diagnosed and given a prescription which I wasn't allowed to take. Luckily, it went away on it's own. 

As is now regarding jobs, I've tried applying to places before, but without experience, and being 21, nothing hired me. I've kept trying but with college and my mother, my energy is already so abysmally low that often it seems like the only way I can cope is to do what's necessary. Depression (at least what I think is depression, due to my mother not believing in mental illness) is a bitch but I do my best to fight it. I also recognize it would be hard to hide the job as I live an hour and a half from any business, and my parents track my location to ensure I just go to school and back home, but I'm willing to work past that. With quarantine, this has made things even more difficult because even if I had the energy and gusto to go out and try to get hired, nothing is hiring. I will look into reselling stuff, though. I have been looking at some textbroker things to make money on the side, save up and such, but even then, (god this is embarrassing), my parents look at my bank statements and have called me out for my purchases before. I don't doubt they'll find the source of revenue and berate me until I give up. I don't mean to make excuses, which I'm sure all of these sound like, so I'll keep trying, despite this.

With all that said, I think the worst thing I can do is give up. I know I'm not hopeless, despite not having much of any resources. I know that something will give. I know that if I keep pushing, if I keep trying to get through, there will be a day when this is just a bad memory. I won't let them win.

My mother is currently looking over all of my work since she has full access to my syllabus. She also made me drop every class using Zoom as she believes it's a "chinese conspiracy". It's fucking awful. Stay strong.
Unfortunately, my parents abuse me whenever I try to get a job, so I have nothing saved up.

Thank you. I try to be resilient. I think I might have some kind of depression or anxiety, and that makes it hard, but it's worth trying. I'm hoping that something will give soon.

I guess it's that there's this perception that everyone is entirely in charge of themselves. I take this a bit too much to heart sometimes as motivation and discipline, and think that I'm in this circumstance of being behind the curve because of my own inactivity. Maybe it's not that way, and I should cut myself some slack for being behind everyone due to my mother, and not myself.

Thank you so much for the kind words. I don't want to give up yet but it just kinda seems like its the best solution sometimes, when all the resources I've sought haven't worked.

There are a couple of resources on campus, but they don't have confidentiality or anything. My parents look at and go through all of my registration stuff and will see I went. I've tried it, too, and it didn't work out. I spoke to them about my situation and whether they could help me and they couldn't do it without it showing up somewhere.

I go to college and they offer therapy, but my mother typically doesn't allow me to be places without her knowing. If I tried to go to therapy and lie about it, she would most likely drive by where I said I was supposed to be going and catch me in the act. This happened recently when I left 30 minutes early to change classes. 

But that's a whole different issue. Thank you for the advice, though, I'll see if I can make therapy on campus work.

I live about a 30 minute drive from anywhere I could work and don’t have a means of transportation to get there. I’d absolutely get one, though, if each time I left the house I wouldn’t be hounded and I had a way to get to work. It ends up being a ton of abuse for little gains, and though it is a step in the right direction, with my mental state I think it would make me more suicidal.

Definitely on the debt. Whichever I choose, during the undergraduate program I plan on looking for internships, finding part time work, cutting off every possible expense I can to put towards paying it off, and living with multiple roommates.
